claims.conditions: A person invokes the skill for work too large for one agent session, in a repository whose issue tracker the agent is permitted to write to (or with the skill's local-markdown fallback), and that person or a teammate is available for the tickets the skill marks human-in-the-loop.
claims.rationale: The source plans work as one 'map' issue with child decision tickets and blocking relationships (lines 21, 114), says to 'never resolve more than one ticket per session', research tickets excepted (line 105), and requires a session to claim a ticket before working it (lines 67, 123). Its frontmatter sets disable-model-invocation: true, and it states that a human-in-the-loop ticket 'only resolves through that live exchange; the agent never stands in for the human's side of it' (line 75); its default output is 'decisions, not deliverables' (line 13). The person therefore starts each use and owns the decisions the map records. Agent-driven parts exist inside that frame: research tickets are resolved by sub-agents (lines 77, 115) and, absent a named ticket, 'you pick the next decision, not the user' (line 120). Side effects are external and visible to collaborators: issues are created, commented on and closed, and research branches are pushed with no pull request (lines 115, 125). Plausible failure modes: a non-interactive ticket is closed on the agent's own resolution with no stated human check; pushed research branches have no cleanup step; the text expects concurrent sessions (line 128) but names only the assignee claim as concurrency control. Falsified if sessions resolve human-in-the-loop tickets without the live exchange.
